meta.title: Proof — Privacy-first CV editor
meta.description: Generate your CV with any AI, proof it in a live editor, and export a flawless PDF. Your data never leaves the browser.

hero.tagline: Open schema · Any AI · Zero storage
hero.body: Download the open schema, drop it into ChatGPT, Claude or any model you like, then import the result. Proof it, style it, and export a flawless PDF — your data never leaves the browser.

aiBand.body: Most builders trap your data behind a form. Proof hands you an open schema and gets out of the way — use the AI you already trust.
aiBand.step1Body: One documented JSON file — the blueprint for a complete CV: identity, experience, skills, the lot.
aiBand.step2Body: Paste it into your AI of choice and describe yourself. No prompt to copy, no model lock-in. You own the conversation.
aiBand.step3Body: Drop the JSON back in. Pick a template, fine-tune, and compile to PDF — entirely on your device.

makeYours.body: A live editor with a real-time PDF preview. Reorder, restyle, and re-compile until every line sits exactly where you want it.
makeYours.feature1Body: Swap layouts instantly — more on the way.

privacy.body: Compilation runs in your browser via WebAssembly. No server, no database, no logs, no account. Your CV — and the AI conversation that made it — stay entirely with you.

openSource.body: Proof is open source. Fork it, add a template, bend the schema to your needs — it's yours. Not a coder? Tell us what's missing and we'll take a look.
openSource.requestSub: Tell us what you need — open an issue
openSource.supportSub: Keep Proof free, private, and ad-free

cta.body: Two minutes from blank page to a PDF you're proud of.

notFound.headline: This page didn't make the cut.
notFound.body: The page you're looking for doesn't exist, was moved, or failed quality control. Let's get you back to something real.

error.headline: Something broke.
error.body: An unexpected error occurred. Your saved CVs are untouched — they live in your browser, not on our servers — so retrying should get you right back to where you were.

onboarding.title: Welcome to Proof
onboarding.subtitle: A privacy-first CV editor. Your data is stored in this browser — nothing is saved server-side.
onboarding.step1Body: Use "+ New" to create a CV from the template, or "↑ Import" to load an existing JSON file. You can have multiple CVs and switch between them.
onboarding.step2Body: Select a template from the list. The middle panel lets you reorder sections, toggle page breaks, and adjust colors, fonts, and spacing.
onboarding.step3Body: Hit "Generate PDF" in the editor panel. Your CV is compiled with Typst and the PDF appears in the preview. Download whenever you're happy.
onboarding.sharedComputerNote: Data will be stored in session storage and cleared automatically when this tab closes.
onboarding.confirmEnablePrivate: This moves your saved CVs into this tab's temporary storage. They'll be permanently deleted as soon as you close this tab. Continue?
onboarding.confirmDisablePrivate: This saves your CVs to this browser's permanent storage, where they'll persist after you close the tab. Don't do this on a shared or public computer. Continue?

terms.metaDescription: What Proof does and does not do with your data.
terms.title: Privacy & Terms
terms.subtitle: Plain English. No legalese.
terms.s1p1: Your CV data is stored exclusively in your browser's localStorage. It never leaves your device except during PDF generation (see below). We have no database, no user accounts, and no server-side storage of CV content.
terms.s1p2: If you clear your browser storage, your CV data is gone. There is no cloud backup. We recommend downloading your CV JSON periodically using the Download button in the editor.
terms.s2p1: When you click "Generate PDF", your CV data never leaves your device. The Typst compiler runs entirely in your browser as a WebAssembly module (~6 MB, downloaded once and cached). Compilation happens locally; no CV content is sent to any server at any point.
terms.s2p2: The only network requests are: loading the compiler itself (from this site), loading fonts (also from this site), and the analytics beacon described below. Your CV data is never included in any of these requests.
terms.s3p1: This site uses GoatCounter for basic traffic analytics. GoatCounter collects page views, referrer URLs, browser type, and country — no cookies, no fingerprinting, no personal data, no cross-site tracking.
terms.s3p2: GoatCounter is open source and its privacy policy is available at goatcounter.com/help/privacy.
terms.s4p1: Proof sets no cookies. Layout saves and CV data are stored in localStorage, which is not a cookie and is never transmitted to the server automatically. GoatCounter also sets no cookies.
terms.s5p1: Proof is open source. You are welcome to inspect the code, self-host it, or contribute. The source code is the most authoritative description of what the tool actually does.
terms.s6p1: If anything material changes — particularly around data handling — this page will be updated. The date below reflects the last revision.

forLlms.metaDescription: Complete CV JSON schema and layout/style reference for Proof. For LLMs and agents generating CV data.
forLlms.title: Schema Reference
forLlms.intro: Complete reference for generating valid Proof data. Covers the CV content JSON, layout structure, and all style parameters for each template. Intended for LLMs and agents producing CV files for import.

section1.heading: 1 · CV JSON schema
section1.intro: The CV is a single JSON object. All sections are optional except identity. Text fields in highlights, description, and summary support Markdown-style links: [text](https://url).
section1.contactNote: The visual editor's own type picker only offers 6 of these (no medium or facebook) — writing JSON directly gets you the full set above.

section2.heading: 2 · Available section IDs
section2.intro: These are the built-in section IDs that the editor and templates know about. The sidebar template can also render any of these in the left column.

notes.core_strengths: string[] of short strings, rendered as pills. Available on every template — not sidebar-only. Section title is translated (en/es/de/fr).
notes.leadership_profile: single object, not an array: { subtitle?, highlights? }. No title/name — renders under a fixed, translated heading.

section2.customNote: Custom sections: any top-level key not listed above is rendered generically under a heading made from the key name. Supported shapes: a plain string; a string[] (rendered as bullets); an array of objects with title (or name)/subtitle/period and either highlights (string[]) or description; or a single object (not an array) with subtitle and either highlights or description — the same shape leadership_profile uses.

section3.heading: 3 · Layout JSON structure
section3.intro: When you generate a PDF from the editor, a layout JSON is compiled alongside the CV data. You can also produce layout JSON directly to control section order, columns, and per-section spacing.

fields.header: Always required as {"style": "split" | "stacked"} — the import validator rejects any other value — but only the default template actually reads it, toggling between a side-by-side and a stacked name/headline/contact header. Every other template (minimal, modern, sidebar, and the rest) has a single fixed header layout and silently ignores this field, so pick either value for them; it has no visible effect.
fields.sections: Array of main-column section entries (see below).
fields.sidebar_sections: Sidebar template only. Array of sidebar section entries.
fields.style: Style overrides (see §4). Applied on top of template defaults.

fieldsEntry.breakable: Whether Typst may insert a page break before this block. Default: true.
fieldsEntry.pre_spacing: Space above the section title. Overrides template default.
fieldsEntry.post_spacing: Space below the section rule. Overrides template default.

fieldsColumns.type: Must be "columns" to activate this variant.
fieldsColumns.content: Array of column contents; each element is an array of section IDs for that column.

section4.heading: 4 · Style parameters
section4.intro: Style values live in the style key of the layout JSON. All are optional — omit any to use the template default.
section4.commonNote: section_pre / section_post aren't in a shared param list technically — every template declares them individually — but all 10 use the same range shown above except sidebar, which widens both (see its own table below). headline_size and section_rule_gap are template-specific, not universal; see the per-template table next.
section4.accentHeading: accent_color — every template, different default per template
section4.accentIntro: All 10 templates declare an accent_color param under this exact key — it's not shared/universal in the schema sense (each template sets its own range and default), but every template has one. 7 of the 10 also have headline_size (8–14pt, default 10) — all except minimal, sidebar, and editorial. section_rule_gap (0–0.5em, default 0.2) exists on only default, sidebar, and timeline.

bannerPurpose.header_bg: Dark band header background — banner only

section4.sidebarNote: Sidebar also widens its shared section_pre/section_post ranges: 0.2–1.5em (default 0.5) and 0.05–0.8em (default 0.2) respectively, instead of the 0.2–0.9 / 0.05–0.4 every other template uses.

sidebarPurpose.sidebar_link_color: Links and icons in the sidebar
sidebarPurpose.sidebar_ink: Name and entry-title colour in the sidebar

section4.exampleHeading: Style embedded in layout — example (banner template)
section4.exampleNote: header.style is still required by the schema even though banner ignores it (see §3) — pick either value.

contactTypes.title: Collect contact types carefully
contactTypes.body: Use the exact type strings (email, phone, location, linkedin, github, medium, facebook, web). The "key" field is the display label — it can be anything ("Email", "E-mail", "Work email" all render fine). The "value" for linkedin/github should be the full URL or just the path (both work).

summaryParagraphs.title: summary uses \n\n for paragraphs
summaryParagraphs.body: The summary field is plain text. To create multiple paragraphs, separate them with a double newline (\n\n). Single newlines are treated as spaces.

tags.title: Tags are decorative pills
tags.body: The "tags" array on experience, side_projects, and certifications renders as small grey pills at the bottom of the entry. Keep them short (1–3 words). For certifications, the special tag "expired" renders a warning style.

links.title: Links work anywhere in text fields
links.body: highlights, description, and summary all support [text](url) Markdown links. You can also link to another section in the PDF with [text](#section-id) — e.g. [see my projects](#side_projects).

omit.title: Omit sections you have no data for
omit.body: All top-level sections except identity are optional. Omitting them entirely is cleaner than including empty arrays.

subtitle.title: subtitle is flexible
subtitle.body: There is no strict format for subtitle. Common conventions: "Company · Location" for experience, "Degree · Field" for education, "Issuer · Year" for certifications. The · separator is just a display convention.
